identity.title: The ALMA Fornax Cluster Survey I: stirring and stripping of the molecular gas in cluster galaxies
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first results of the ALMA Fornax Cluster Survey (AlFoCS): a complete ALMA survey of all members of the Fornax galaxy cluster that were detected in Hi or in the far infrared with *Herschel*.

evidence.quote: Although accurate distance measurements are available for some of the AlFoCS galaxies, here we adopt the distance to the Fornax cluster (19.95 Mpc, (cite: Tonry2001)) as a common distance to all galaxies.

question.value: Does the cluster environment affect the molecular gas in Fornax cluster galaxies, and which processes are responsible?

evidence.quote: The goal of this work is to investigate whether the cluster environment indeed affects the molecular gas in galaxies, and if so, attempt to identify which processes are mainly responsible for this.
observations of the $^{12}$CO(1-0) line in 29 AlFoCS targets were carried out under project 2015.1.00497.S (PI: Timothy Davis)
an already reduced image of NGC1365 was taken from the ALMA archive (project ID: 2015.1.01135.S, PI: Egusa, Fumi)
Band 3 observations were performed between the 7th and 12th of January 2016

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: SPW3 on 12CO(1-0), 1.875 GHz, 3840 channels; other SPWs 128 channels, 2 GHz for continuum

evidence.quote: The bandwidths are 1.875 GHz, covering 3840 channels. The other spectral windows, covering 128 channels each with total bandwidths of 2 GHz, were used to target the band 3 continuum
The CO(1-0) rotational line (rest frequency: 115.271 GHz) was observed to create spatially resolved maps
ALMA’s 12 m configuration was used, which has a primary beam size of $\sim$55” at $\sim$115 GHz.
The largest recoverable scale is 25”.
Typical rms noise levels are around $\sim$3 mJy/beam.
It was observed on 20 March 2016.

analysis_steps.goal: Make moment maps, PVDs and spectra

method.value: Masked moment method with smoothed-cube mask clipped at 3 or 4 sigma; PVD from beam-wide slit along major axis

evidence.quote: Gaussian smoothing was applied to a copy of the data cube, in both spatial axes as well as the velocity axis, with a full width at half the maximum (FWHM) of 1.5 times the beam’s major axis

key_parameters.value: velocity smoothing 4 channels; clip at 3 or 4 sigma

evidence.quote: where $x$ is chosen to give the best visual result, and equals 3 or 4.

method.value: Visual inspection of moment 0 and 1 maps: regular vs disturbed

evidence.quote: Whether a galaxy is morphologically disturbed or regular is determined by visual inspection of the moment 0 and 1 maps

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line flux and derive H2 masses

method.value: Gaussian fit or direct box integration; M_H2 from CO flux with metallicity-dependent X_CO (Accurso+2017), metallicity from stellar mass

evidence.quote: For the first group we fit a Gaussian to the CO(1-0) line and integrate this fit to obtain the total line flux. For the second group, we integrate directly under the line observed.
Here we assume a distance from the main sequence $\Delta$MS = 0 for all galaxies.

evidence.quote: It is multiplied by $2.14 \times 10^{20}$ to obtain X$_\text{CO}$ (cite: Bolatto2013).

method.value: 3 sigma limits assuming Gaussian line of FWHM 50 km/s, peak 3x rms in inner PB-corrected cube

evidence.quote: we assume Gaussian line profiles with FWHM of 50 km s$^{-1}$

method.value: Compare M_H2/M_star with xCOLD GASS median relation (log interpolation/extrapolation); deficiency = log observed - log expected; KS and Mann-Whitney tests vs. cluster radius

evidence.quote: We define H$_2$ deficiencies here as log($M_{H_{2}, \text{observed}}$) - log($M_{H_{2}, \text{expected}}$).
Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Mann-Whitney *U* tests are unable to reject the null hypothesis that both groups of galaxies are drawn from the same distribution at more than $\sim$2$\sigma$.
calibrated manually using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package (CASA, version 5.1.1

used_for.value: Mopra baseline fitting and SDFITS conversion

evidence.quote: `LIVEDATA` is used to fit baselines and transform the raw datafiles to SDFITS files.
`GRIDZILLA` is then used to combine these files into data cubes.
The spectra were reduced using the 2dFDR software package
spectral classifications and redshifts were determined using MARZ
CO was detected (at $> 3 \sigma$) in 15 of the 30 galaxies observed.
Galaxies with regular CO emission have an average H$_2$ deficiency of -0.50 dex
galaxies with disturbed CO emission have an average H$_2$ deficiency of -1.1 dex
The resulting metallicity, assuming these relations hold, is $12 + \text{log}(\text{O/H})$ = 8.12 (or 0.27 $Z_\odot$).

findings_qualitative.value: All 8 detected galaxies with M* < 3e9 Msun have disturbed molecular gas; 7 regular galaxies

evidence.quote: All 8 detected galaxies with stellar masses below $3 \times 10^9 M_\odot$ have disturbed molecular gas reservoirs, only 7 galaxies are regular/undisturbed.

findings_qualitative.value: Detections and non-detections occur at all projected cluster locations

evidence.quote: Both detections and non-detections occur at all projected locations in the cluster.

claims.hypothesis: Cluster environment disturbs molecular gas, especially in low-mass galaxies
claims.experiment: Visual classification of CO moment maps for 15 detections, compared with HI of field dwarfs (LITTLE THINGS)
claims.result: All galaxies below 3e9 Msun disturbed; only ~half of field dwarfs disturbed in HI
claims.finding: Low-mass galaxies are more disturbed than in the field; Fornax still active

evidence.quote: this indicates that these low mass galaxies are more disturbed than their counterparts in the field.

claims.hypothesis: Fornax galaxies are H2 deficient relative to field

evidence.quote: AlFoCS galaxies with disturbed molecular gas reservoirs are therefore, with few exceptions, significantly deficient in H$_2$ compared to their counterparts in the field

claims.hypothesis: Ram pressure stripping disturbs the molecular gas
claims.experiment: Look for tails aligned with cluster centre
claims.result: Two tails (MCG-06-08-024, ESO359-G002) aligned with cluster direction
claims.finding: RPS possible but not confirmed; galaxy-galaxy interactions not excluded

evidence.quote: Based on these data alone, it is difficult to say whether it is ram pressure affecting these galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Gas properties depend on cluster location
claims.experiment: Deficiency vs projected distance with KS and Mann-Whitney tests
claims.finding: No clear dependence on location, small sample

evidence.quote: appears to be independent of the galaxy’s location within the cluster. However, the sample size is small.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting used to recover extended emission and maximise S/N at cost of resolution

evidence.quote: Many of the sources have extended emission, and using natural weighting will help ensure that this is recovered in the data.

limitations_admitted.value: Current HI data lack resolution to compare HI and CO morphologies

evidence.quote: The current Hi observations available are not of sufficient resolution to do this.

referee_caveats_inferred: Disturbed/regular classification is purely visual and subjective
Single distance of 19.95 Mpc applied to all galaxies
X_CO from stellar-mass metallicity with Delta MS = 0 is uncertain for dwarfs
xCOLD GASS control sample lies above the mass range of most disturbed dwarfs; extrapolation used
25" maximum recoverable scale may resolve out flux in extended galaxies
